transcript.text: Start by reading the files. for f in ['chart.py','summary.txt','table.csv']: print('=====',f); print(open(f).read()) continue

chart.py has two faults that match the diagnosis. 1. **Swapped data.** The axis labels say x is GDP per capita and y is electricity access rate, but the data is passed the other way round. The scatter uses x=ElectricityAccessRate and y=GDPPerCapita. The annotation positions are swapped the same way. I will swap both back. 2. **Wrong title.** The title talks about Urban Population. summary.txt says the title is "Relationship Between GDP per Capita and Electricity Access Rate (2018-2023)", so I will use that exact text. Nothing else will change. I will also print part of table.csv and check the axes and title on the figure itself. with open('table.csv') as f: print(f.read()[:600]) s = open('chart.py').read() s = s.replace(""" x=df['ElectricityAccessRate'], y=df['GDPPerCapita'],""", """ x=df['GDPPerCapita'], y=df['ElectricityAccessRate'],""") s = s.replace("xy=(subset['ElectricityAccessRate'].mean(), subset['GDPPerCapita'].mean())", "xy=(subset['GDPPerCapita'].mean(), subset['ElectricityAccessRate'].mean())") s = s.replace("'Correlation Between Urban Population and GDP per Capita (2018-2023)'", "'Relationship Between GDP per Capita and Electricity Access Rate (2018-2023)'") with open('chart.py','w') as f: f.write(s) import matplotlib.pyplot as plt plt.close('all') exec(compile(s,'chart.py','exec')) ax = plt.gca() print(ax.get_title(), ax.get_xlim(), ax.get_ylim()) continue
